bead.title: claude-tui: implement Harness+Account+Quota turn execution over internal/pty with intermediate ProgressEvents
bead.description:
PROBLEM: The claude-tui skeleton from child #1 has no real turn-execution path. ADR-013 §3 requires that claude-tui drive the Anthropic CLI through internal/pty/ and emit intermediate tool_call/tool_result ProgressEvents DURING the turn (not at Stop), via PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks. Subscription billing is observed off the live CLI session, so the wire format must be the interactive PTY surface.

ROOT CAUSE:
- The existing claude harness uses --print and only emits a Final ProgressEvent on subprocess termination; ADR-013 mandates mid-turn events for claude-tui.
- internal/pty/ exists but is not driven by any harness yet; session-pool, /clear-between-turns, and orphan-reaper concerns from ADR-013 are unimplemented for this harness.
- AccountHarness and QuotaHarness need CLI-observed signals (identity, usage) instead of API-metered numbers; existing helpers live in the neutral anthropic/ package after child #1.
- Per testing concern in ADR-013, loop overhead beyond inference must stay under 10ms and wall-time-per-turn must stay within 2x of claude --print on equivalent prompts.

PROPOSED FIX:
1. Implement claudetui.Harness.RunTurn: open or reuse an internal/pty/ session, write the prompt, drive readers, terminate on the CLI's end-of-turn marker, return Final event.
2. Install PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook handlers that emit tool_call and tool_result ProgressEvents on the harness event channel as they fire mid-turn.
3. Implement a session pool keyed by working directory: between turns issue /clear; on shutdown reap any orphaned PTY processes.
4. Resolve hook-conflict concern from ADR-013 by routing claude-tui's hooks through the existing conflict-arbitration layer (no new mechanism).
5. Implement AccountHarness.Identity off CLI auth status output (parsed via anthropic/ helpers).
6. Implement QuotaHarness.Quota off CLI quota observation surface (parsed via anthropic/ helpers).
7. Add a benchmark that compares per-turn wall time against a claude --print baseline on a shared canned prompt and asserts the ratchet.

NON-SCOPE:
- ModelDiscoveryHarness implementation and no-static-fallback enforcement (child #3).
- Capability baseline rows, evidence IDs, ADR-013 status promotion (child #4).
- Cassette-driven static fallback for production code (forbidden by fizeau-89eca738).
- Service-side changes beyond what child #1 already wired.
- Redesigning the hook-conflict arbitration layer; reuse existing infrastructure.

Depends on child #1. Governing artifacts: ADR-013 §3, CONTRACT-004, internal/pty/ library.
bead.acceptance:
1) TestClaudeTuiTurnEmitsIntermediateToolEvents asserts that for a prompt that triggers a tool use, the harness event channel yields at least one tool_call ProgressEvent before the Final event, and that every tool_call is followed by a matching tool_result.
2) TestClaudeTuiSessionPoolReusesAndClears asserts /clear is issued between consecutive turns sharing a working directory and that the underlying PTY session is reused (same pid).
3) TestClaudeTuiOrphanReaper asserts that on harness shutdown any leftover PTY child processes are reaped within a bounded timeout.
4) TestClaudeTuiHookConflictRouting asserts claude-tui's PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks register through the shared conflict-arbitration layer and coexist with user-defined hooks without duplication.
5) TestClaudeTuiAccountIdentity asserts AccountHarness.Identity() returns the CLI-observed account string parsed via internal/harnesses/anthropic helpers.
6) TestClaudeTuiQuotaObservation asserts QuotaHarness.Quota() returns CLI-observed usage parsed via internal/harnesses/anthropic helpers.
7) BenchmarkClaudeTuiTurnWallTime asserts mean wall-time-per-turn is within 2x of the claude --print baseline on the shared canned prompt, and that loop overhead beyond inference is under 10ms.
8) go test ./... -count=1 is green.
9) lefthook run pre-commit is green.
